items.title: Section: Skilful With Every Designation, and Five Kinds of Immeasurable Beings a Bodhisattva Learns to Guide

items.zh: 如實知故，一切安立皆得善巧。從此尋求、於此尋求、由此尋求。既尋求已，由此究竟皆正安立，如是名為一切安立皆得善巧。於諸安立得善巧故，復於教授能得善巧。
items.en:
Third, designations and the rest; first, establishing designations; first, stating skilful mastery overall. Because he truly knows, he becomes skilful in every designation.
Second, explaining through investigation and the rest. Investigating from this, investigating regarding this, investigating by means of this — having thus investigated, this culminates in every designation being correctly established; this is called skilful mastery of every designation.
Second, the five kinds of immeasurable; first, skillfulness in instruction. Being skilful in designations, one further attains skillfulness in instruction.

items.title: Section: The King of Concentrations, Sixteen Bodhisattva Titles, and the Bodhisattva Virtues Chapter Closes

items.zh: 於其教授得善巧故，復能獲得無量所緣三摩地王。獲得如是三摩地已，能不唐捐宣說正法種種行相，說正法時皆有勝果。能於大乘究竟出離。以依大性而出離故，能攝大乘。由此復於彼彼大乘出離位中。得彼彼名。一切菩薩同共此名，一切世間諸佛菩薩皆共安立、皆共稱歎。當知是名所可稱讚功德殊勝。
items.en:
Second, attaining that equipoise. Being skilful in instruction, one further attains the king of concentrations over immeasurable objects.
Third, the fruit and benefit of teaching. Having attained such concentration, one teaches the true dharma in every aspect without waste, yielding excellent results whenever the dharma is taught.
Fourth, encompassing the nature of the Great Vehicle. Through complete transcendence achieved in the Great Vehicle, relying on its own great nature, one encompasses the Great Vehicle entirely.
Fifth, the bodhisattva's own titles. By this, at each respective stage of transcendence within the Great Vehicle, one attains each respective title; all bodhisattvas share these names in common, established and praised alike by every buddha and bodhisattva throughout the world.
Second, concluding. Know this is called the excellence of praiseworthy qualities.

items.title: Section: Five Marks of a True Bodhisattva, and Fifteen Kinds of Heightened Aspiration

items.zh: 由得如是殊勝名故，當知獲得諸菩薩相，諸相所相，成就其相。如是正行一切種相，在家、出家二分菩薩所能成辦。於二分中能成辦已，正行堅固，於諸善品獲得一向增上意樂。如是意樂，或在家品所應攝受，或出家品所應攝受。
items.en:
Second, marks and the rest encompassed; first, marks. By attaining such excellent titles, one attains the genuine marks of a bodhisattva, marked by these very marks, accomplishing this mark.
Second, division. Such complete practice in every respect is accomplished by both lay and renunciate bodhisattvas.
Third, heightened aspiration. Having accomplished practice in both divisions, practice made firm, one attains a single-minded, heightened aspiration towards every wholesome quality; such aspiration belongs to both lay and renunciate bodhisattvas.

items.title: Section: The Retrospective Closes — Twelve Abodes, Five Rebirths, and the Entire Bodhisattva Stage's Own Architecture Explained

items.zh: 或於善品能正安立，乃至安住。從此已上，故作意思受諸有生，於彼生處常得值遇諸佛菩薩。及能起作一切有情諸饒益事。恒常無間，蒙佛菩薩無倒教授，任持善品，領受殊勝證得分位。由領受故，於可稱讚攝受殊勝證得分位，能正安處，如己舍宅。住此位已，能於後後殊勝分位，一切種相覺慧昇進，漸次乃至到於究竟，於其中間不生喜足。如是昇進，證得究竟，從此不求其餘上地。已到究竟極邊際故，名得無上。是名菩薩地義次第。
items.en:
Fourth, abodes. Rightly establishing every wholesome quality, and abiding therein.
Fifth, rebirth. From this ground onward, one deliberately takes rebirth wherever needed, always encountering buddhas and bodhisattvas there.
Sixth, being received. One undertakes every beneficial deed for beings.
Seventh, grounds. Constantly and without interruption receiving undistorted instruction from buddhas and bodhisattvas, upholding wholesome qualities, receiving one's excellent, attained stage; by this reception, one dwells securely in this praiseworthy, excellent, attained stage, as if in one's own home.
Eighth, conduct. Abiding in this stage, one progressively advances in wisdom of every kind through excellent stage after excellent stage, all the way to the very end, never resting content along the way.
Third, encompassing establishment. Thus advancing, reaching ultimate completion, one seeks nothing beyond, having reached the very outer limit; this is called attaining the unsurpassed.
Second, concluding. This is called the sequential meaning of the Bodhisattva Stage.

items.title: Section: New Ground at Last — the Stage With Residue Remaining Opens, the Sixteenth of Seventeen Stages

items.zh: 如是已說菩薩地。云何有餘依地？當知此地有三種相。一者、地施設安立，二者、寂靜施設安立，三者、依施設安立。云何地施設安立？謂有餘依地，除五地一分，謂無心地、修所成地、聲聞地、獨覺地、菩薩地。除一地全，謂無餘依地。所餘諸地，名有餘依地。是名地施設安立。
items.en:
Within the basic section, the Stage With Residue Remaining, the sixteenth.
Thirteenth, the Stage With Residue Remaining; first, concluding what precedes and generating what follows. Thus the Bodhisattva Stage has been explained. What is the Stage With Residue Remaining?
Second, correctly distinguishing the stage's characteristics; first, stating. Know that this stage has three characteristics.
Second, listing them. First, the establishment of the stage; second, the establishment of tranquility; third, the establishment of what is relied upon.
Third, explaining; first, the establishment of the stage; first, posing the question. What is the establishment of the stage?
Second, explaining. The Stage With Residue Remaining excludes a portion of five stages — the stage without mind, the stage brought about by cultivation, the Śrāvaka Stage, the Pratyekabuddha Stage, and the Bodhisattva Stage — and excludes one entire stage, the Stage With No Residue Remaining. All the remaining stages are called the Stage With Residue Remaining.
Third, concluding. This is called the establishment of the stage.
Commentary: as for excluding a portion of five stages — this means excluding, from each of the five stages, the portion belonging to nirvāṇa without residue remaining, and taking the remaining portion to establish the Stage With Residue Remaining. As with the stage without mind, there are two establishments: if the store consciousness has been permanently extinguished, this is called the stage without mind belonging to no residue remaining; if only the arising consciousnesses of that occasion have ceased, this is called the stage without mind belonging to residue remaining. The same meaning applies, as is fitting, to the stage brought about by cultivation, the Śrāvaka Stage, the Pratyekabuddha Stage, and the Bodhisattva Stage.

items.title: Section: The Arhat's Four Kinds of Tranquility — Even Aṅgulimāla, Struck by Stones, Remains Undisturbed

items.zh: 云何寂靜施設安立？謂由四種寂靜，施設安立有餘依地。一、由苦寂靜故；二、由煩惱寂靜故；三、由不損惱有情寂靜故；四、由捨寂靜故。云何苦寂靜？謂阿羅漢苾芻諸漏永盡，所有當來後有眾苦皆悉永斷，已得遍知。如多羅樹斷截根頂，不復現前。由得當來不生法故，是名苦寂靜。云何煩惱寂靜？謂阿羅漢苾芻貪欲永斷、瞋恚永斷、愚癡永斷，一切煩惱皆悉永斷。由得畢竟不生法故，是名煩惱寂靜。云何不損惱有情寂靜？謂阿羅漢苾芻貪欲永盡、瞋恚永盡、愚癡永盡，一切煩惱皆悉永盡，不造諸惡，修習諸善，是名不損惱有情寂靜。云何捨寂靜？謂阿羅漢苾芻諸漏永盡，於六恒住，恒常無間多分安住。謂眼見色已，不喜不憂，安住上捨，正念正知。如是耳聞聲已、鼻嗅香已、舌甞味已、身覺觸已、意了法已，不喜不憂，安住上捨，正念正知。是名捨寂靜。即依如是四種寂靜，說有餘依地最極寂靜、最極清涼，是名寂靜施設安立。
items.en:
Second, the establishment of tranquility; first, posing the question. What is the establishment of tranquility?
Second, stating. The Stage With Residue Remaining is established through four kinds of tranquility.
Third, listing them. First, tranquility of suffering; second, tranquility of affliction; third, tranquility of not harming beings; fourth, tranquility of equanimity.
Fourth, explaining; first, tranquility of suffering. What is tranquility of suffering? An arhat monk, every outflow permanently exhausted, has permanently severed every future suffering of rebirth, having attained complete understanding. Like a palm tree with its root and crown both severed, never to sprout again — having attained the dharma of never being reborn, this is called tranquility of suffering.
Second, tranquility of affliction. What is tranquility of affliction? An arhat monk has permanently severed greed, hatred, and delusion — every affliction entirely severed — attaining the dharma of never arising again; this is called tranquility of affliction.
Third, tranquility of not harming beings. What is tranquility of not harming beings? An arhat monk, every affliction entirely exhausted, commits no evil at all, cultivating only what is wholesome; this is called tranquility of not harming beings.
Fourth, tranquility of equanimity; first, posing the question. What is tranquility of equanimity?
Second, stating. An arhat monk, every outflow permanently exhausted, constantly and without interruption abides for the most part in the six ever-abiding states.
Third, explaining. Seeing form with the eye, feeling neither joy nor sorrow, abiding in supreme equanimity with correct mindfulness and correct awareness; likewise hearing sound, smelling scent, tasting flavour, feeling touch, and cognizing phenomena with the mind, feeling neither joy nor sorrow, abiding in supreme equanimity with correct mindfulness and correct awareness.
Fourth, concluding. This is called tranquility of equanimity.
Fifth, concluding. Depending on these four kinds of tranquility, the Stage With Residue Remaining is said to be utterly tranquil and utterly cool; this is called the establishment of tranquility.

items.zh: 云何依施設安立？謂有八種依。

blocks.text: The retrospective closes, and with it the Bodhisattva Ground. Then a short new stage begins: the sixteenth, the "stage with remainder" (有餘依地), describing an arhat who still has a body.
Venerable Miào Jìng: thought starts from names; the four investigations yield the four kinds of genuine knowledge (Day 409).

Venerable Miào Jìng: compassion, kind speech, and the rest come down to compassion, great wisdom, and courage. Master Cháng Bǎi: only with all five is one a genuine bodhisattva. Heightened aspiration, Venerable Miào Jìng: lay and renunciant bodhisattvas alike can accomplish it.

Master Cháng Bǎi: deliberately considering where to benefit beings, one is reborn there. Venerable Miào Jìng: the ultimate truth is the bodhisattva's own house; they live there. "Ground" means a level of attainment, gradually traversed.

It covers the earlier stages, except part of five of them and the whole of the stage without remainder. Venerable Miào Jìng: while the store consciousness remains, there is "remainder". Master Cháng Bǎi: the arhat's example is the attainment of cessation.

Of suffering, of affliction, of not harming beings, and of equanimity. Venerable Miào Jìng: hence it speaks of future suffering, not present. Master Cháng Bǎi: it does not exclude present bodily pain. On equanimity: Venerable Miào Jìng, the mind clings to nothing, good or bad. Master Cháng Bǎi: mindful and wisely aware of it, not numbness.

Aṅgulimāla, once a murderer, became an arhat; struck by stones on his alms round, he remained undisturbed. The tranquillity of an arhat does not mean pain never comes; it means the mind is not bound by it.

quiz.q: "Investigating from this, regarding this, by means of this." Which practice do the lectures name?
options: the four investigations: from name, then thing, then both; yielding four kinds of genuine knowledge
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: thought starts from names; the four investigations yield four kinds of genuine knowledge. Master Cháng Bǎi: "regarding this" investigates the thing named.

quiz.q: What does "king" mean in "king of concentrations"?
options: mastery: entering, abiding, and emerging freely

quiz.q: "Attaining the marks of a bodhisattva." What traits do the lectures name?
options: compassion, kind speech, etc.; Miào Jìng: compassion, wisdom, courage; Cháng Bǎi: all five make a genuine bodhisattva
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: compassion, kind speech, and so on — compassion, great wisdom, and courage. Master Cháng Bǎi: only with all five is one a genuine bodhisattva.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "single-minded heightened aspiration"?
options: it means attaining patience towards non-arising
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: heightened aspiration means attaining the patience towards non-arising; lay and renunciate bodhisattvas alike can accomplish it.

quiz.q: "Deliberately taking rebirth, always meeting buddhas." How do the lectures explain it?
options: Cháng Bǎi: he considers where he can benefit beings and goes; Miào Jìng: in absorption he sees buddhas; every place is a buddha-world
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: deliberately considering where to benefit beings, one is reborn there. Venerable Miào Jìng: entering absorption, one sees the Buddha; everywhere is a buddha-world.

quiz.q: "Dwelling as in one's own home." What is the bodhisattva's home, says Venerable Miào Jìng?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the ultimate truth is his own house; he lives there.

quiz.q: When is one called "attaining the unsurpassed"?
options: having reached the very outer limit, seeking nothing beyond
quiz.why: Having reached the outer limit, one seeks nothing beyond. Master Cháng Bǎi: "ground" means a level of attainment, gradually traversed.

quiz.q: How is the Stage With Residue defined?
options: all stages, except a portion of five and the whole of the No-Residue Stage
quiz.why: Excluding a portion of five and all of the No-Residue Stage. Venerable Miào Jìng spells this out.

quiz.q: Taking the mindless stage, how do the lectures split the "portion"?
options: only with the store consciousness ended is it no-residue; Miào Jìng cites dreamless sleep, Cháng Bǎi the attainment of cessation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: while the store consciousness remains, there is residue; dreamless sleep is an example. Master Cháng Bǎi: the arhat's example is the attainment of cessation.

quiz.q: Through which four tranquilities is the stage established?
options: suffering, affliction, not harming beings, equanimity
quiz.why: Tranquility of suffering, of affliction, of not harming beings, and of equanimity.

quiz.q: Why does tranquility of suffering speak only of future suffering?
options: arhats still have bodily pain now; only future rebirth is ended
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: hence it says future, not present. Master Cháng Bǎi: it doesn't exclude present bodily pain.

quiz.q: "Six ever-abiding states." How do the lectures explain tranquility of equanimity?
options: the six faculties meeting objects in equanimity; Miào Jìng: mind clings to neither; Cháng Bǎi: mindful, and aware of being mindful
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the mind clings to nothing, good or bad. Master Cháng Bǎi: mindful, and wisely aware of it — not numbness.
